children: The first full quarter after the merger records higher patient volumes, improved occupancy and growth in complex clinical procedures across the combined hospital network

Aster DM Quality Care Limited reported a 19 per cent year-on-year increase in revenue to Rs 2,829 crore in Q2 FY2027, for the quarter ended 30 September 2026, while normalised profit after tax (PAT) rose 34 per cent to Rs 281 crore. The healthcare provider also recorded a return on capital employed (ROCE) of 23 per cent, improving by 152 basis points year-on-year, marking its first full quarter as a combined entity following the merger of Aster DM Healthcare and Quality Care India.

The company served 2.2 million patients during the quarter, registering 12 per cent year-on-year growth. Hospital occupancy improved by 335 basis points, from 65 per cent to 68 per cent, supported by higher patient volumes and increased utilisation across its network.

Robotic surgeries increased approximately 39 per cent, kidney transplants grew 31 per cent, and joint replacements recorded 29 per cent growth. Medical Value Travel (MVT) volumes also increased 31 per cent year-on-year, while MVT revenue grew 36 per cent, supported by demand from the Maldives and Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) markets.

Commenting on the performance, Varun Khanna, Managing Director and Group CEO, said higher patient volumes, greater clinical complexity and a favourable payor mix contributed to the revenue and profitability growth. He also highlighted the integration of people, processes and systems following the merger, alongside the company's unified culture initiative, GO GREATER, launched across nearly 40 locations.

During the quarter, CARE Banjara in Hyderabad performed its first adaptive Deep Brain Stimulation procedure for Parkinson's disease management. Aster Medcity, Kochi, also performed Kerala's first liquid nitrogen cryoablation for breast fibroadenomas.

The company launched three Centres of Excellence: the ARISE Robotic Spine Institute at Aster CMI, Bengaluru; CARE Cancer Institute at Ramkrishna CARE, Raipur; and the Fetal Medicine Centre of Excellence at Aster Medcity, Kochi.

In H1 FY2027, mature hospitals contributed approximately 73 per cent of hospital revenue, recording 18 per cent year-on-year growth. Emerging hospitals, including Kasargod and Nagarcoil, registered growth of 62 per cent.

Executive Chairman Dr Azad Moopen said the combined entity would continue investing in clinical talent, infrastructure and technology. The company is also progressing its Aster Trivandrum project towards commissioning.
